interactions.title: Hralgar recalls Apollyon and the Omnis Pura
lines: DM: "I will enjoy your company for the evening before I depart. Should there be anything you wish to discuss, please. I would enjoy the company, or companionable silence if that's what you would prefer."
DM: He looks over towards Delwath cooking. He takes a deep breath and sort of leans back, sort of in anticipation, just waiting patiently for whatever happens next.
Kenzo: By this point Kenzo's broken his meditation, and has has taken his staff, and has been carving into into his staff. And then says to Hralgar,

Kenzo: "Hralgar, it would be an honor before the break—before the dawn breaks, and you depart— to continue to learn more of your story. I— I've written what I remember, and look forward to writing more. So I hope to continue to hear more of your journeys and your your adventures. I think, for all of us, we're concerned about Apollyon and the Drankorian era that you were in. That seems still to be connected to what's unfolding in today's time. And it might benefit all of us to learn more of what you've seen and understood of that time, because those insights seem relevant now."
DM: So he he turns to Kenzo and he says,
DM: "I— I spent much of my younger days not caring for humans, uninterested in their presence across the land. It is easy not to notice them.
DM: And in those days Drankor was— the Empire was a force for peace. It was the the Golden Age. I guess it's always hard to see the best times when you're in them."
DM: I did have visitors sometimes who came up to the mountains to share their stories.

DM: But after the Civil War, sort of stopped caring for the humans. The chaos down on the plains below, Drankorian fighting Drankorian, and— what difference did it make to me? High in the sky above them, up in the mountains?
DM: Still gathered news sometimes, and the Stoneborn, the dwarves— in those days the kingdom of Ardith was powerful and learned.
DM: Many dwarfs would come visit me. We would talk of magic in the past, and the sky above and the deep dark below.

DM: Those were also good days, but maybe not for the humans, and it was only later, maybe a 100 years or more after the end of the Civil War, after many Drankorian emperors had died in battle to the east— began to venture again across the plains.
DM: It was then that I was— and he looks sort of around.
DM: This tower happened to me during Apollyon's reign. I I know little of him other than not all, not all in Drankor agreed with his reign.
DM: But he had a— he had a way with words. He had a— the magic too, and he pulled many to his side. And he was the most successful emperor in battle in 50 years, and that pulled many more.

Kenzo: Can you say more of how he was so successful in battle? Why— what what strategies? Was he using special magic? How was he able to achieve such such great victory over such a long period of time?
DM: He was skilled in magic beyond any I had seen.
DM: He had a tower, a laboratory, a place in the ocean, south and west of Drankor that even the winds and the storms could not penetrate. No news ever came to me of that place.
Kenzo: Was this a perfectly circular island by chance?
DM: I think it was something like that. Yes.
Kenzo: And you never went yourself?
DM: Something of his magic kept the winds away, kept the storms away.
Kenzo: If we were to try to go there, do you know, or have any advice or thoughts on how we might be able to— have you heard of anybody that's gone there?

DM: He sort of closes his eyes. I know not who may have traveled there long ago. People came and went. Ships sailed there. The humans, the the Drankorians of these plains, they were—they were never really my chief interest.
DM: I only saw what news the winds brought, and what passed across these plains and blew into the mountains, or what I saw as a passing storm on the wind.

DM: Did not care for their politics and conflicts. Wasn't like it was in the early days when the scholars of Drankor would humbly approach to ask my favor and advice. So they turned away. I turned away.

Kenzo: You know, of Apollyon's strength, you mentioned his magic. Was he—was it a a magic that he had acquired himself, or was he using powerful items? Is there—do you know more about the source of his power?
DM: I know little of— know little of how he became emperor, or—
DM: There was a— the Drankorians loved societies of all kinds, clubs and organizations, secret and not, civic groups and magical societies.

DM: There was one that that Apollyon was important, and—or the leader of, called the Omnis Pura. They were— know not really where they came from, but they had f—or discovered, somehow acquired some powerful magic.
DM: And believed that they were the pinnacle of all creation, putting themselves above the elder races, even the first children of Aldanor, giants and the dragons.
Seeker: What form did this powerful magic that they discovered take?
DM: I think this was part of Apollyon's skill in battle, his war mages.
DM: You know, do not know if this was new magic, but young races are always rediscovering things that we have known forever. You know this as a dwarf, I am sure. Of them.
DM: Those—and and you, Delwath, must know this. The humans come and go so quickly they forget and find something, find something again and again and again, thinking it new each time.
Seeker: They delight in learning like children.
DM: They have no memory of the past, no sense of the future.
Seeker: And yet this club and Apollyon's power persist, so perhaps they did discover something big this time.
DM: Perhaps. Was never my concern. Even they cannot change the weather.

before: DM: So as as you are all scattered across camp, Hralgar walks forward, and you can feel, Kenzo, in your meditation, Seeker in your fiddling with your books, Wellby with his eyes closed, Delwath cooking, Riswynn praying—you can feel the earth shake every time Hralgar steps. And at his full height is about 25–30 feet tall. Like nearly that. This—

DM: The the ship itself, having been excavated and dragged out of the earth by Hralgar, is, is maybe 50 feet off the ground, but reaching over his hand, Hralgar can reach the top of this ship. And for you, it's this massive cliff.

DM: And you know, in there is something about his physical presence. Most of the time you've interacted with him and been in the dreamscape, and somehow he didn't, he didn't seem quite so looming and towering over everything when you were in his dreaming. Just the very fact when he sits down near you to listen, you're still looking 15 feet up to his worn, tired face.

DM: You can see he has—he has long, scraggly white hair that's disheveled. Water still drips off the back of his head from the rainstorm which hasn't seemed to, despite it clearing up, the rain hasn't seemed to quite pass over him. There's still some thing of the storm lingering on him. His eyes are blue white. He's got a sort of unshaven, unkempt beard.

DM: And as he leans forward, bringing his head closer to you—his head substantially bigger than most of you, only Kenzo, and maybe Delwath at would even, you know, match the size of his head— as he leans in listening, and says quietly for him, but in a booming voice that echoes with a hint of thunder:
after: Seeker: Who.
Seeker: Hralgar, I've been studying some of these books that we rescued from the tower before you rightly returned it to dust.
Seeker: One of them is written in your tongue, as far as I can tell. Tales Before the Fall, it's called.

Seeker: And I pull out from behind me a book that is, I think, twice as tall as I am. Actually, it's it's some effort that I lever it up so that you can look at the cover, and then stand up, ask for Wellby's help, holding up the other end and wrench open the cover to lift it around so that we can see the frontispiece.
Seeker: None of us can read Giant, I'm afraid. You think there's anything of interest in here? Would you be willing—

interactions.title: Tales before the separation of the planes
lines: Seeker: Hralgar, I've been studying some of these books that we rescued from the tower before you rightly returned it to dust.
Seeker: One of them is written in your tongue, as far as I can tell. Tales Before the Fall, it's called.

Actually, it's it's some effort that I lever it up so that you can look at the cover, and then stand up, ask for Wellby's help, holding up the other end and wrench open the cover to lift it around so that we can see the frontispiece.
Seeker: None of us can read Giant, I'm afraid. You think there's anything of interest in here? Would you be willing—
Delwath: Oh, I can read Giant.
DM: He looks at it, and he says, 'Hmm!'

DM: I do wonder where Eudomes came by such a book. It is not uncommon among the amongst the giants, although few of our works are written, because it is a tale of the legendary histories of our people from the age of creation.

DM: A story of the elder Titans and the empires of our times that stretched across— he looks around—all this land that you can see, and far beyond as well, before any of your kind set foot on this land.
Seeker: And what is the fall referred to in the title?
DM: A— fall is maybe not how I would translate that word. Separation.
DM: Once, long ago, when the world was young, the planes that we know now—elemental planes, the Feywild—were not separate from the world.
DM: But Aldanor, when they made the firstborn of the elder races, separated the worlds.
DM: And much of the magic and power that was in the land was pulled apart to the other planes.
DM: So these are tales from before then. Before humans, before elves, before dwarves.
DM: Before even the gods of your kind walked the earth.
Seeker: And in the time of this rift what happened to the giants? Did they disperse to the among the planes, or are they all here on Taelgar?
DM: Most left, like the dragons and the fey and the elementals. Some stayed, but our empires fell, crumbled without the magic to sustain them.
Seeker: Hmm! Are you personally of an age to remember this?
DM: I was only 500 when I was trapped. I guess I would be over a 1,000 years now. But few of our kind now live more than four millennia, and most less.
Seeker: So you are in your old age now, you're saying?
DM: Few of my kind, anyway.

DM: It is hard to explain. If a hurricane—if you see a hurricane crash into land from the mount—powered by the monsoons of the Green Sea, there is the good chance that is not just a hurricane, but an ancient storm giant who has passed on from the mortal realm.
DM: This is where I plan to go as well. It is not death as you would describe it, but it is something different.
Seeker: It's good to know and comfort, and a comfort to know that you, our friend, will persist in this world in that way.

Delwath: Can I identify languages, or just read them?
DM: You can just make a— an Intelligence check. Mostly you can just read them. But this one is not—would not be easy to identify. Yeah, now, you don't know what it is.
Delwath: What what does it say? I mean, could I tell what way?
DM: Yeah, you can. You can flip through it. I mean, you can see, you know, it's—it seems to be kind of a natural history of sorts of giants. It's clearly a written from a human perspective.

interactions.title: Hralgar explains his phasing stone and hidden instructions
lines: Seeker: We'd like to find this phasing stone he mentioned up the mountains. There any further clues as to how we might find it, and also, how big? That is, this gonna be hard to carry with us? Speaking of carrying things around.

DM: It lets you reshape physics. If it's too big for you to carry, you'll just imagine it smaller.
Wellby: What were phasing stones used for, besides piloting or powering ships like this?
DM: I guess it would depend on who possessed it. Much of— Okay. I mean, the lore.
DM: From long ago. He points at the giant book. If you read that book you'll see long ago, before magic was diluted and all the planes pulled apart, they could do anything.
DM: If you wanted a feast, you can make a feast. If you wanted to be—be 30 feet tall, you could be 30 feet tall. If you wanted instead to be a sparrow flying through the sky, you could be a sparrow.
Kenzo: But not in a vision, like an actuality?
DM: Now, of course, their power is much constrained. Yeah.

DM: Flow of energy through that— he says like a long word in a language you don't understand—that— pipes, I guess, through which magic flows are narrow, restricted, so those that are left, or in my day those that were left, were always attuned to specific purposes.
DM: So the one I had—the one that I hope for your sake is still in my ancient home—I used to provide food and drink for my guests. But with some effort it can be retuned to fly the airship.
Seeker: And what process does this retuning involve?

DM: If you reach my palace, my former home, the— the lower floor of that building was once my library, and study. The light that shone through the skylights illuminating—it's quite pretty in the—when the morning snow fell in, twinkled in the light.
DM: If you can find that place in the center of the library, there's a vast stone pillar stretching maybe 80 feet, going from top to bottom of the floor.
DM: And if you channel lightning magic into this pillar, runes will appear, runes that well, describe how to construct the controls of a sky ship and embed the phasing stone in them.
DM: I do not recall now the details, and so I wrote them down.

DM: He looks at Seeker and Riswynn. Between the 2 of you, I have full faith you can follow my instructions, if if any of you can read Giant, I guess. Did not think to carve my instructions in Dwarvish, unfortunately. I hope that will not be an insurmountable barrier.
Seeker: It seems our elf is literate in Giant.

Might be missing. If you can find it, it tells the story of Vindristjarna, the Star of the Wind, this ship that's crashed.

DM: It is my notes and collections of stories that people told me, as I sought to understand the history of my people in these lands. That may be of interest to you as well, although again, I— I know not what has survived these past 1,000 years. Although I would be surprised if my stone has fallen.
Seeker: The— among my people, we say it is always advisable on purchasing a new skyship, be sure to buy [garbled], a record of any previous ownerships, and especially accident.
DM: He chuckles slightly and says, 'Well,'—who looks? He looks to his right. There's some significant accidents in the history of this particular airship.
Seeker: I look forward to learning all of its quirks.

DM: Please.

Kenzo: We're curious again, just to share with you these. Do you know of ways in which powerful artifacts could, in fact, be destroyed? interactions.title: Destroying artifacts with elemental fire
lines: Kenzo: We're curious again, just to share with you these. Do you know of ways in which powerful artifacts could, in fact, be destroyed? We believe that Apollyon is gathering artifacts now, or employing his his minions to do so, and we're concerned about them falling into the wrong hands. Do you know of ways to destroy powerful magic?
DM: Powerful magic can be destroyed by other powerful magic.
Kenzo: He was going to say something like that.
DM: What you would like to destroy?
Riswynn: Some advice came to us that a volcano's heat perhaps would suffice to destroy magical objects.
DM: Some volcanoes are echoes of when the plane of fire was connected to this world. The magic of the plane of fire would suffice to destroy many artifacts, indeed.
Wellby: We're seeking to destroy the artifacts that belonged to Apollyon, and survived his passing.
DM: That sounds like a great quest. But not my quest. What would you like to know?
Riswynn: Can we describe where we think the one volcano we know of is, and ask if that's a— he knows that that's that?
DM: Well, you know the volcano way to the East that Kenzo saw is definitely connected to the plane of fire, because Kenzo talked to somebody from the plane of fire, he said, this is my volcano.
Riswynn: Okay, so are there—why don't we start with that one, like there's one very far in the East.

Riswynn: There is a volcano very far to the East that we know is connected to the Plane of Fire, as you describe. We wonder if there are other similar locations that we have not yet learned of, that you—

DM: The solid and static heat and flame of a volcano is not so much my domain. My cousins, the Fire Giants, would know better. Some once lived east of here long ago, but I have no idea if they are still there or not, or if they would even deign to speak with humans or any of the other younger races.
Kenzo: Might you be able to make an introduction?
DM: Not tonight, and I won't be here tomorrow, but I do know something of volcanoes.

DM: The north coast of the Green Sea, where I grew up in my childhood— many of the islands that the sea people there lived on are volcanic, and there— chain of volcanoes runs all the way across the north, across the the mountains that were the the home of a loose collection of tribes and small kingdoms on the northern border of Drankor stretching all the way across the central mountain range to land of fire and ice, a mountain chain running east and west.

DM: And that same ring of volcanoes continued across the Green Sea, then cutting across the island. It was called Erelion in my day. I know not if it is still called such, a large island in the middle of the Green Sea.

DM: And south and west of here, many of the islands in the Nevos Sea are volcanic. Could not tell you which of these volcanoes may be a remnant of this connection to the Plane of Fire; but should you wish to search for volcanoes, that is where I would start.
Riswynn: The islands and the seas, and—
Wellby: The question of seas makes me wonder: if you travel due east across the Green Sea, is there a far shore?
DM: Not even my people know the answer to that.
DM: Should you really wish to know what is far beyond the horizon in the ocean, have to speak with the merfolk.
Wellby: I'm adding it to the side quest list.
Delwath: It's totally. You say you will not be here tomorrow, but as the wind, could you not send an omen to the Fire Giant?
DM: I know not even if these giants still live east of here. If I pass that way, and I see them, perhaps the omen of my passing will echo in their dreams.
